what_it_does: Modern AI chips are built from multiple smaller die-like pieces (chiplets) glued together with high-speed links. These links need clock signals that switch between active and idle modes to save power. When switching from idle back to active, the sudden power surge can cause the voltage to dip, which throws off the timing of data signals—like trying to read a document when the lights flicker. This chip uses a 'matched-delay' technique: it adds compensating delays to clock paths so that data timing stays locked and correct even when voltage droops during the mode transition, preventing bit errors.
